scorecards.inningsCommentary: Bangladesh commenced their first innings at Zahur Ahmed Chowdhury Stadium, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 68 from Mushfiqur Rahim, complemented by a commanding 105-run stand between Sabbir Rahman and Mushfiqur Rahim that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.69 RPO. Australia's bowling response was spearheaded by Nathan Lyon (8/94), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Concluding at 305/10 (113.2 ov), Bangladesh posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Australia began their reply under scoreboard pressure, tasked with responding to Bangladesh's opening innings total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 123 from David Warner, complemented by a commanding 152-run stand between PSP Handscomb and David Warner that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.14 RPO. Bangladesh's bowling response was spearheaded by Mustafizur Rahman (4/83), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Reaching 377/10 (119.5 ov), Australia's innings completed the first-innings exchange (72 Runs (Australia)), shaping the strategic contours for the second half of the Test.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Australia embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 86 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. GJ Maxwell anchored the innings with a resolute 25, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. Mustafizur Rahman (1/16) maintained tight lines for Bangladesh, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Reaching 87/3 (15.3 ov), Australia successfully completed a historic fourth-innings pursuit to seal an emphatic victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Zahur Ahmed Chowdhury Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Bangladesh posted 305/10 (113.2 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Australia countered with 377/10 (119.5 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 8-Wicket Spell: Nathan Lyon (8/94), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Nathan Lyon delivered a masterclass for Australia (14 Wickets), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Australia 62%) and allowing Australia to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Bangladesh faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Australia's bowling unit, bolstered by David Warner (131 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Australia won by 7 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Australia's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Bangladesh produced fighting phases, Australia won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
